questions.stem: The main metabolic cell body of a neurone containing nucleus and Nissl's granules is named:
questions.explanation: The Cyton (Soma) is the cell body of a neurone.

questions.stem: Nissl's granules present inside cyton and dendrites are composed of:
options: B) Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum and Ribosomes
questions.answer: B) Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum and Ribosomes
questions.explanation: Nissl's granules consist of RER clumps and free ribosomes for protein synthesis.

questions.stem: Nissl's granules are strictly ABSENT in which part of a motor neurone?
questions.explanation: Nissl's granules are absent in the axon hillock and axon.

questions.stem: Saltatory action potential impulse conduction leaps along myelinated axolemma specifically at:
questions.explanation: In myelinated axons, action potentials jump from Node of Ranvier to Node of Ranvier.

questions.stem: Which CNS neuroglial cell extends perivascular end-feet to construct the Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB)?
questions.explanation: Astrocytes form perivascular feet constructing the Blood-Brain Barrier.

questions.stem: Which neuroglial cell synthesizes myelin sheath around axons inside the Central Nervous System (CNS)?
questions.explanation: Oligodendrocytes form myelin sheaths in CNS; Schwann cells form myelin in PNS.

questions.stem: Phagocytic macrophage defense neuroglia residing in the Central Nervous System are:
questions.explanation: Microglia are phagocytic macrophages in the CNS.

questions.stem: Sensory pseudounipolar neurones featuring a single process dividing into peripheral and central branches reside in:
options: C) Dorsal Root Ganglia (DRG) of spinal nerves
questions.answer: C) Dorsal Root Ganglia (DRG) of spinal nerves
questions.explanation: Pseudounipolar sensory neurones reside in spinal Dorsal Root Ganglia.

questions.stem: Mature post-mitotic human neurones lose the ability to undergo cell division post-birth due to absence of active:
questions.explanation: Mature neurones lack active centrioles, rendering them post-mitotic.

questions.stem: Direction of nerve impulse transmission across a typical multipolar neurone is:
questions.explanation: Nerve impulses travel centripetally along dendrites to cyton, then centrifugally down the axon.
